notes: A DATE YOU TYPED IS ACCEPTED OR REFUSED — NEVER QUIETLY MOVED. If you changed the date on a saved draft to a day outside every open accounting period, the draft saved without complaint, and you only discovered the problem when you tried to post it — after filling in the whole voucher. Nothing was ever recorded wrongly; the check simply came at the wrong moment. It now happens when you save, and tells you what to do: open that period, or pick a date inside one that is open. WHY IT HAPPENED. The routine that decides which period an entry belongs to serves two callers with opposite needs. A REVERSAL takes a date the system chose and must land somewhere sensible, so when no period accepts it the routine returns the nearest period with the date moved into it. A person typing a date is the other case: moving it silently is worse than refusing, because you would never learn the entry is not where you put it. The draft-editing code read the period and discarded the moved date, leaving a draft whose date and period disagree. They are now compared. WHAT IS UNCHANGED. Re-dating a draft into a DIFFERENT open period still moves the draft to that period and posts normally. No data changes in this release. Back up before installing, then install over the top.
